title: Adapt the Same Experience to a New Question
status: New proposed Lesson 06 production script, 2026-10-30. No new animation or narration in this handoff.
learningOutcome: Select different relevant evidence from the same experience for a changed follow-up, without changing its facts, ownership or uncertainty.

scenario.kind: Explicitly fictional authored training case, not a learner biography or a real admission interview

facts.text: Three volunteers prepared a one-page visitor guide for a community open afternoon.
The case participant drew the map. Maya listed session times. Noah assembled the guide.
The day before the event, the participant noticed that the map said Studio B while Maya's schedule said Blue Room.
The participant did not know whether those names meant the same room and asked the event coordinator rather than guessing.
The coordinator confirmed that both names referred to the same room and that its door sign said Blue Room.
The participant changed the map label to Blue Room and told Maya and Noah. Maya checked the schedule; Noah assembled the updated guide.
During the event, the participant saw one visitor use the map to find Blue Room.
There was no visitor survey or total count of people helped. No comparison shows what would have happened without the change.
In reflection, the participant would agree a shared list of room names earlier next time. This is a proposed future change, not an action already taken.

unknowns: Whether anyone else used the map successfully
Whether a visitor would have found the room without this change
Whether the guide made the whole event successful
How long checking with the coordinator took
Any awards, numerical impact, leadership appointment or wider achievement
scenario.permittedDecisionReason: Conflicting labels could confuse visitors; confirming the door-sign name avoided choosing a name without checking. This is the participant's stated reasoning, not a measured causal result.

roles.maya: Follow-up partner in a later authored rehearsal; also the schedule volunteer within the remembered case
roles.noah: Guide assembler within the remembered case

boundaries: Do not invent new case events, timings, quotations, achievements or causal outcomes.
Keep own actions distinct from Maya's and Noah's work.
Clearly label the model as fiction; never insert it into a real learner's personal response.
A private learner may rehearse an ordinary truthful experience, choose another topic or use this labelled fictional case for language practice.
No recording, AI scoring, truth verification, upload or success inferred from a click.
No rigid answer length or required STAR script; these are optional planning distinctions, not official assessment criteria.

blocks.title: Change the selection, not the history
A useful limit is still an answer
Carry the method into your account

L06.S07.c001.speaker: coach
L06.S07.c001.text: A follow-up can change what the listener needs without changing what happened. Keep the same facts, then select the part that answers this question. You do not need a fresh story for every question, or the whole story every time.
L06.S07.c001.visualEn: Full-screen board. Retain Fictional worked example on the source bank. Three question tabs sit above fixed fact cards; moving a pointer changes selection, not the facts. No characters.
L06.S07.c001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S07.c001.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S07.c002.speaker: coach
L06.S07.c002.text: For the visitor-guide case, compare these questions: What did you contribute? What would you change next time? How much did the guide help? They ask for an action, a proposed improvement, and evidence of impact. Those are different requests.
L06.S07.c002.visualEn: Show the three questions as separate editable labels. Reveal matching Action / Proposed change / Impact evidence lanes without filling learner notes. Keep numbered case sources available in the DOM panel.
L06.S07.c002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S07.c002.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S07.c003.speaker: coach
L06.S07.c003.text: For contribution, bring forward drawing the map, checking the conflicting names, and changing its label. Keep Maya and Noah beside their own work. Shortening the account should not turn a shared task into a claim that one person did everything.
L06.S07.c003.visualEn: Move F02/F04/F06 cards into the Action lane while leaving Maya: schedule and Noah: assembled guide visible at normal legible contrast. Same cards retain their IDs; no duplication into personal ownership.
L06.S07.c003.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S07.c003.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S07.d001.speaker: learner
L06.S07.d001.text: Next time, I would agree a shared list of room names earlier. That could help us check the map and schedule before assembling the guide, rather than noticing the mismatch the day before.
L06.S07.d001.visualEn: Brief model answer card headed Fictional worked example / Proposed change. No past-event reenactment of a shared list being made. Use a dashed future card, not a completed tick. Characters may remain offstage.
L06.S07.d001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S07.d001.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L06.S07.c004.speaker: coach
L06.S07.c004.text: That answer stays in the future. It connects the proposed change to the mismatch, without claiming the new process has already worked. Do not quietly move a good idea from the reflection card into the history of the event.
L06.S07.c004.visualEn: Return to board; proposed list stays right of a labelled Future boundary. A ghost arrow toward Past stops without implying that the action occurred. Preserve F09 wording.
L06.S07.c004.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S07.c004.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S07.d002.speaker: learner
L06.S07.d002.text: I saw one visitor use the map to find Blue Room. We did not collect a total or survey visitors, so I cannot say how much the guide helped overall.
L06.S07.d002.visualEn: Authored model card in Impact evidence lane. One visitor observation card only; no audience crowd, percentage or success chart. Show No overall measure as text, not a red failure state.
L06.S07.d002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S07.d002.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L06.S07.c005.speaker: coach
L06.S07.c005.text: This answers the impact question with the evidence available. It does not prove that changing the label caused that visitor to find the room. A precise limit can make an account clearer than a confident statement the facts cannot support.
L06.S07.c005.visualEn: Place observation and causal inference on separate cards. Keep causal inference tagged Not established. Do not imply the visitor would otherwise have been lost.
L06.S07.c005.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S07.c005.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S07.c006.speaker: coach
L06.S07.c006.text: If you prepared your own account, try one different follow-up now. Select relevant details you can honestly describe; leave other details available for later. If you are using the fictional case for language practice, keep that label. A model gives you a way to practise, not a personal history.
L06.S07.c006.visualEn: Replace case board with an unfilled private planning surface. Keep model bank separately labelled and collapsed, not copied into the personal area. No mic or submit button.
L06.S07.c006.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S07.c006.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S07.c007.speaker: coach
L06.S07.c007.text: Before answering, notice what is being asked. Then make your contribution, reasoning, evidence and uncertainty clear where they matter. You can pause, clarify a question, or say that you do not remember a detail. The aim is an understandable account you can stand behind.
L06.S07.c007.visualEn: Final calm board: Question / Relevant facts / Honest limits. Retain white space; no badge, score, automatic course completion or invented future-course preview. Offer ordinary Replay and Next section or Back to lesson controls as applicable.
L06.S07.c007.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L06.S07.c007.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L06.S07.h101.purpose: Let the viewer locate which known facts address each question; no response is inferred.
L06.S07.h101.visualEn: Hold fixed fact bank and questions. No automatic check mark or completed answer state.

L06.S07.h102.purpose: Compare action, future proposal and limited impact evidence while preserving the same fact bank.
L06.S07.h102.visualEn: Settle all three lanes with equal visual weight. No best-person score, progression reward or inferred learner achievement.

boundary: Use formal explanation and short explicitly fictional examples. Model events are not learner biography. No inferred recording, truth verification, official rubric or wider outcome.
